content:
arun: Heads-up — canary p99 jumped right after today's kernel-autoselect + microbatch-hysteresis change. Seen on blue-cluster canary nodes, affecting long-seq requests (>=1024). Approx 11:03 UTC. trace=abc123

arun: Quick snapshot from the metric chart (canary, 10%):
```
p95: 120ms -> 130ms
p99: 260ms -> 980ms
requests_affected: ~0.6%
avg_seq_len_affected: 1400
kernel_selected: matmul-vec32 (fallback) instead of fused-attn
```

tony: link to dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/canary/blue (looks like tail only on >1k seq) :eyes:

maya: I profiled a couple of samples w/ perf-trace — seeing KV cache churn and big memcpy spikes. Suspect hysteresis caused kernel rebinds mid-request, evicting KV pages.
```
hotspot: kv_cache_evictions/sec  420 -> 3100
memcpy_ms (per-step)         0.8 -> 5.4
context_switches             200 -> 560
```

julia: deploy-bot shows rollout details: kernel-selector=aggressive (new heuristic), microbatch_hysteresis_ms=8. Canary started at 11:00Z. Should we fast-back it?

deploy-bot: Deploy deploy-98123 rolled out to canary (10%) at 2026-03-18T11:00:12Z by @julia. Changes: runtime.kernel_selector=aggressive, runtime.microbatch_hysteresis_ms=8

ken: I'm going to do a fast rollback for canary to stop the tail spike. Planning: cancel rollout + restore kernel_selector to stable-heuristic.
ken: running:
```bash
redwoodctl rollout cancel --id deploy-98123 --target canary
redwoodctl config set runtime.kernel_selector=stable-heuristic --target canary
```
ken: applied rollback commands, waiting for pods to restart (watching 3/3 healthy)

arun: Thx. Also flagging that KV cache threshold might need to be lifted for long-seq flows, hysteresis of 8ms led to too-frequent kernel flips under microbatch coalescing.

ken: canary rollback complete at 11:06Z — kernel_selector back to stable-heuristic, microbatch_hysteresis reverted to 3ms for canary.

ken: immediate metric update: p99 for canary down to ~280ms within 90s of rollback.

arun: Confirmed on traces: tail latency back to baseline, KV evictions dropped to ~450/sec. Closing canary incident. Will open follow-up to tune hysteresis and KV thresholds.

julia: Filing follow-up ticket: ENGRT-2048 — investigate hysteresis thresholds + kernel affinity for long sequences, include perf-run and canary replay. Assigning to eng-runtime.

sre-bot: Alert cleared for canary-p99-spike (incident-id=inc-20260318-11:03).

maya: quick note — we should add a guard in kernel-selector: prefer 'pinned-fused' for seq>=1024 to avoid rebinding. I'll draft a PR. :+1:

tony: Thanks team — nice fast backout. Keep the replay data in the ticket.
